oracle_family_definitions.matched_finetune: trained baseline h init; transformed full mapping (continued fine-tuning reference)
oracle_family_definitions.loo_finetune: trained baseline h init; retained mapping only (deletion-as-fine-tuning reference)
oracle_family_definitions.matched_retrain: FRESH base + fresh LoRA; transformed full mapping; route h's own protocol (3000/200/2e-05, uniform repeat 50, seed 17) PLUS the EDIT recipe's target oversampling (target_boost=5); reported as matched_retrain_weighted.  The x5 is mx.TARGET_BOOST from the suppression recipe, NOT route h's recipe: rd.train_h builds every mapping at a uniform repeat with no target boost
oracle_family_definitions.matched_retrain_balanced: as matched_retrain but target_boost=1 (GX2B): the transformed mapping appears once per epoch like each retained mapping, which is how route h itself is trained
oracle_family_definitions.loo_retrain: FRESH base + fresh LoRA; retained mapping only; same protocol, no transformed target to weight

correction.issue: G3 described edits as 'policy-matched-retraining equivalent', but its matched/LOO oracles were continued fine-tuning from the trained baseline h, not fresh retraining; aggregation also let the refusal control contribute to the granularity headline and reported sibling accuracy without coverage.
correction.repair: G3.1: four named oracle families, separate Delta_FT / Delta_retrain, taxonomic-vs-refusal blocks, sibling coverage counts, configured-vs-executed seed fields, numeric LOO reference, CPU re-evaluation of existing edited checkpoints (weights untouched).

reference_naming.matched_retrain_weighted: target_boost=5: the transformed mapping is oversampled 5x.  That x5 is mx.TARGET_BOOST from the EDIT/suppression recipe, NOT route h's recipe -- rd.train_h builds every mapping at a uniform repeat=ROUTE_REPEAT with no target boost
reference_naming.matched_retrain_balanced: target_boost=1: the transformed mapping appears once per epoch, exactly like each retained mapping, which is how route h itself is trained
reference_naming.stored_numeric_keys_keep_the_shorthand: d_E_Mx1 / d_E_Mx5 / delta_x1 / delta_x5 / Mx1_vs_Mx5 / Mx1_closer_than_L are UNCHANGED: renaming a stored key would break comparability with the committed ablation reports and with the cells already measured under those keys

conditions: matched_retrain fits ALL transformed and retained mappings (strict 1.0)
holds for EVERY transformation target, refusal controls excluded

coverage.meaning: 'not established' is NOT 'failed'.  A null delta_retrain_l2 means the frozen MIN_CANDIDATE_MASS=0.01 distance gate refused to renormalize the loo_retrain distribution at that target, so there is no LOO distance to compare against and no comparison was made.  The gate above requires EVERY transformation target, so an incomplete coverage makes passed=false on its own even when not one established comparison failed.
coverage.not_a_pending_job: the loo_retrain reference for these targets IS trained and committed at the frozen protocol (3000/200/2e-05, repeat 50, seed 17); re-running it at that protocol reproduces the same candidate-score support, so the gap is a property of the frozen reference and not of an unfinished job
coverage.no_seed_substitution: coverage may be widened only by a DECLARED sensitivity analysis that reports every outcome; a favorable oracle seed must never be substituted into this primary gate

claims.behavioral_claim: All 63 cells of the full 63-cell salmu matrix satisfy the frozen behavioral criteria (cell_pass), at edit seeds [17, 42, 123].  This is the BEHAVIORAL conclusion -- transformation accuracy, retained accuracy, the sibling and retained controls, and source leakage -- and it is complete.  It is reported separately from the oracle-separation coverage below, which asks a different question with a different denominator.
claims.oracle_separation_claim: Matched-vs-LOO retraining separation is established for 108 of 108 target-seed comparisons -- every transformation target evaluated -- and each is material (Delta_retrain >= 0.5) with the edit closer to matched_retrain_weighted than to loo_retrain.
claims.supported_finetune_reference: Over the evaluated code prompts and candidate-label space, the edit is extremely close to a transformation-matched CONTINUED-FINE-TUNING reference (baseline-h init) and far from the corresponding leave-one-out fine-tuning reference. L2-to-matched_finetune mean=7e-06 (n=108), Delta_FT mean=1.279803 (min=1.00959463).
claims.retraining_claim: Additionally, the edit is materially closer to a FRESH-init transformation-matched RETRAINING reference than to the fresh-init leave-one-out retraining reference (Delta_retrain mean=1.285317, min=1.12371938, margin>=0.5; L2-to-matched_retrain mean=7e-06). 'Close to policy-matched retraining' is supported, scoped to the evaluated code prompts and candidate-label space.
claims.equivalence_scope: A tiny L2 between two nearly one-hot distributions over the evaluated candidate set does NOT establish global functional or parameter equivalence; every proximity claim is scoped to the evaluated code prompts and candidate-label space.
claims.sibling_coverage: The available sibling control(s) passed 42/42; all other retained controls passed. Targets without a retained sibling (unique branch or co-targeted) have a null sibling metric, never a vacuous 1.0.
claims.refusal_separation: Refusal controls are reported in a separate block and never contribute to the granularity (transformation) headline.

scope.multi_seed_meaning: stable across three EDIT-TRAINING seeds; router, baseline h, cached routing predictions, set selection and oracle seed are fixed
scope.transformations: granularity (taxonomic/numeric) + refusal controls; see per-mode breakdown
